record.narrative: I request 12 feature_009-focused comparisons that are currently untested. These are more scientifically urgent than additional broad screens because H60 is the only accepted finding so far and it concerns feature_009 level_001 versus level_003 on outcome_007. H61 and H62 test the intermediate level pattern on the outcome where the association was found: level_001 versus level_002 and level_002 versus level_003. These will distinguish a localized level_001 effect from a gradient or from a level_003-specific pattern. H63, H64, and H68-H75 test whether the same feature_009 level_001 versus level_003 contrast appears across other stable dependency-score outcomes with reasonably large absolute means. For H63 and H64 the registered direction is positive, so a raw negative association with level_001 would appear as a negative signed estimate; for H68-H75 the direction was chosen negative so that a raw lower dependency score in level_001 than in level_003 appears as a positive signed estimate. These comparisons are not independent confirmations of generalizability; they are within-dataset consistency and specificity checks. I avoided feature_009 follow-up on outcome_014 and outcome_006 because their near-zero means make relative 10% inference unstable. I deferred H50 and outcome_007 context controls H76-H78 because the highest-value question is whether the accepted feature_009 signal is specific to outcome_007 or broad across dependency scores, and whether level_002 is intermediate. All returned estimates will be interpreted as already signed to the registered claim direction and judged against approximately 10% of the outcome mean, with valid cell sizes required for each comparison.

Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.

Predictor names and text categorical values use opaque labels. Levels are nominal labels, not ordered numbers. Numeric values, outcome scales, and missingness are preserved.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.

expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep

with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.

Predictor names and text categorical values use opaque labels. Levels are nominal labels, not ordered numbers. Numeric values, outcome scales, and missingness are preserved.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Your action now: Propose scientifically useful new comparisons or refinements for later analysis.

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.

Predictor names and text categorical values use opaque labels. Levels are nominal labels, not ordered numbers. Numeric values, outcome scales, and missingness are preserved.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct

comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.

expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).

If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;

evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.

evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.

record.narrative: The 12 new discovery results mostly reduce the number of competing explanations for H79 while revealing one secondary borderline lead. For outcome_001, H80 and H81 are high-prevalence binary controls and are clinically and statistically null; their intervals are wide but centered near zero. H83 and H84 are also not clinically meaningful: H83 is positive but below the approx 0.0415 10% threshold, and H84 is negative and below threshold in magnitude. H82 is the most promising outcome_001 alternative: its signed estimate is +0.0514, about 12% of the absolute outcome_001 mean, but its interval crosses zero and is wide, so it is deferred rather than accepted or rejected. The feature_009 level-pattern controls on outcome_001 do not support a broad non-level_003 effect: H86 is null, while H85 and H87 are too rare and imprecise to be informative, so their investigations are closed. Thus the remaining feature_009 signal, if real, would be specific to level_001 versus level_003 on outcome_001, but H60's validation failure makes me cautious about accepting H79 without validation. For outcome_008, H88 is essentially exactly at the 10% benchmark (signed +0.0282) and H89 is slightly above it (signed +0.0322), with both intervals excluding zero but not excluding the clinical threshold. These are high-prevalence leads, but they are discovery-only and near the decision boundary, so they are deferred pending validation of the stronger primary lead. H90 and H91 are null and closed. I therefore request independent validation of H79. If H79 validates, it would be the strongest candidate dataset-specific association; if it fails, H89 and then H82 become the next validation priorities.

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.

multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.

comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.

You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short

comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.

expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep

with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.

parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.

is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator

the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.

H112-H116 are the priority robustness and heterogeneity checks: H112 tests outcome_008 feature_008 within the high-prevalence feature_047=1 stratum; H113 tests whether the feature_008 effect on outcome_008 differs by feature_047 status; H114 tests outcome_008 feature_047 within the high-prevalence feature_008=1 stratum; H115 tests outcome_001 feature_023 within the large feature_008=1 stratum; and H116 tests whether the feature_023 effect on outcome_001 differs by feature_008 status. These directly determine whether H89/H88/H82 are more plausibly independent associations or apparent effects arising from a broader correlated high-prevalence predictor pattern. H94-H96 test feature_047, feature_008, and feature_023 on outcome_011, which is a relevant secondary dependency score and helps determine whether the current outcome_008 or outcome_001 leads are outcome-specific or reflect cross-outcome predictor effects. H120-H123 test feature_008 and feature_047 on outcome_003, outcome_004, and outcome_012, further assessing whether these high-prevalence predictors show clinically meaningful effects across additional dependency outcomes or only on outcome_008. All returned estimates should be interpreted in the signed form already supplied by the ledger; for negative-direction claims, a positive signed estimate indicates raw stronger dependency, i.e., a more negative exposed-minus-comparator contrast. These tests are association checks in the supplied dataset and do not establish causality or external generalizability.

Iteration 7/25, stage appraise, attempt 1.
Research goal: investigate which measured predictors and subgroups are associated with scientifically meaningful differences in outcome_012 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_005 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_015 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_002 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_016 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_007 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_013 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_014 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_004 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_009 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_010 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_001 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_008 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_003 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_006 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_011 (CRISPR dependency score). Use the supplied dataset to discover and follow up comparisons, assess effect sizes and uncertainty, and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.

Predictor names and text categorical values use opaque labels. Levels are nominal labels, not ordered numbers. Numeric values, outcome scales, and missingness are preserved.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Your action now: Assess the newly delivered discovery evidence. Optionally set validate to one eligible claim reference for independent validation; omit it for no request. The controller attaches the discovery result. Validation arrives after this stage.

record.narrative: The new discovery results mainly weaken the competing outcome_008 and outcome_001 leads, leaving H89 as the best but still borderline validation candidate. H112 and H113 are structurally uninformative: within feature_047=1 there are no feature_008=0 observations, so feature_008 cannot be evaluated conditional on feature_047; these are unresolved and closed rather than rejected. H114 estimates the feature_047 association within the large feature_008=1 stratum. Its signed estimate is only +0.0113, far below the approximately 0.0282 outcome_008 10% benchmark, and the interval crosses zero. With only 81 comparator observations, I keep H114 unresolved rather than claiming a precise null, but it does not support feature_047 as an association independent of feature_008. Together with the nesting of feature_047=1 almost entirely within feature_008=1, this argues that H88 is likely proxy/confounded with H89, so H88 is deferred and not chosen for validation. For H82, H115 shows the feature_023 effect within the large feature_008=1 stratum is only +0.0299, below the approximately 0.0415 outcome_001 benchmark, although imprecise. H116 is signed for a positive feature_023-by-feature_008 interaction, but the estimate is negative, and the positive-side upper bound is below the benchmark. I therefore reject the registered positive interaction, while noting that the large negative point estimate suggests the overall H82 effect may be driven by the small feature_008=0 complement. This makes H82 less defensible for validation, so it is deferred and closed as a refinement. Cross-outcome screens reduce the likelihood that the high-prevalence features are generically associated across dependency scores: H95, H120, H121, and H123 are rejected because their signed intervals cannot reach the 10% benchmark for the claimed direction; H94, H96, and H122 remain unresolved only because their upper bounds can include clinically meaningful effects, but they are closed because they are not compelling follow-up targets. No claim should be accepted from discovery evidence. I request validation of H89 because it remains the strongest marginal association: outcome_008 with feature_008 1 versus 0 has signed estimate +0.0322 [0.0028, 0.0617], about 11.4% of the absolute outcome_008 mean and CI excluding zero. Its lower bound still falls below the clinical threshold, and its biological specificity is uncertain because feature_047 cannot be cleanly disentangled from feature_008, but if H89 replicates independently it would justify accepting a dataset-specific marginal association. If H89 fails validation, neither H88 nor H82 appears strong enough to justify further validation under the current evidence.

record.narrative: No assessments are due. The evidence base now contains no accepted claims, and the main discovery leads from the saturated outcome_008/outcome_001 searches either failed independent validation or were weakened by correlated-predictor checks and empty structural cells. The most informative next direction is to broaden search to the relatively under-screened outcomes outcome_014 and outcome_006. Their absolute means are near zero, so the approximate 10% absolute-mean clinical benchmark is small, about 0.0093. This makes these outcomes sensitive to modest dependency shifts, but it also increases the risk that borderline discovery signals are statistical artifacts. I therefore registered only predictors with adequate cell counts and high analytical power: feature_030, a nearly universal binary predictor; feature_045, feature_042, feature_065, and feature_052, all binary predictors with roughly 20% to 25% exposed prevalence; and feature_063 level_002 versus level_001, which had adequate prior cell counts on outcome_013. For all claims I used direction -1 to frame the main hypothesis as stronger dependency, i.e. a more negative exposed-minus-comparator score, but anticipated_direction 0 because these predictors have no established biological prior in this dataset. The comparisons are deliberately outcome-pair screens: if a predictor shows a signed estimate near or above the small outcome_014/outcome_006 clinical benchmark with an interval excluding zero, follow-up should examine whether the effect is outcome-specific or part of a broader cross-outcome pattern. Given the multiple comparisons and the small absolute threshold, no new claim should be accepted without a decisive interval, consistency checks, and likely independent validation. All proposed findings remain dataset-specific associations, not causal or generalizable claims.

throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.

and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.

is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum

validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains

retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.

You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using

For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.

The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.

and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.

comparison cell.

hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.

request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.

Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

expectation

and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep

parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.

record.narrative:
I assessed the 12 newly delivered outcome_014/outcome_006 screens. All returned estimates are already signed to the claim direction; because these claims use direction -1, a positive signed estimate means raw exposed-minus-comparator evidence for stronger dependency, while a negative signed estimate means the opposite. The approximate clinically relevant absolute-mean benchmark for these two outcomes is near 0.0093 (10% of the roughly 0.093 absolute outcome means), but this benchmark is small and the screen is heavily multiplicity-prone: 12 comparisons at 95% discovery intervals make borderline near-threshold results fragile. I did not accept any new claim from discovery evidence alone.

The strongest original-direction result is H145: outcome_006 with feature_052 exposed=1 versus comparator=0. Its signed estimate is +0.0412 [0.0008, 0.0816]. The point estimate is large relative to the benchmark, but the lower bound is far below it, and this result came from a multiplicity-heavy screen. It is the best current validation candidate because it is the only original-direction interval that excludes zero, so I request independent validation of H145. If validation is null or lower-bound dominated, it should not be accepted.

Several other results have clinically sized point estimates but intervals that cannot exclude either no effect or subthreshold effect. H136, H139, H140, and H142 are unresolved. H139, H140, and H142 are deferred because their point estimates are clinically sized and they could be followed up if H145 fails validation; H136 is closed because its interval is especially wide and its comparator cell has only 207 observations. H137, H141, H143, and H144 remain unresolved but closed because their point estimates are near zero or their intervals do not prioritize them as follow-up targets. H138 remains unresolved but closed because the point estimate is opposite the claimed direction while the interval still permits a modest positive effect.

H146 is rejected as originally claimed. Its signed interval is entirely negative [-0.0701, -0.0022], which means the raw mean_difference is positive: feature_063 level_002 versus level_001 is associated with a less negative outcome_014 score, i.e. weaker dependency in the claimed strong-dependency direction. Because this is a robust opposite-sign pattern, I registered a reversed refinement with direction +1 for possible future analysis. H147 shows a signed negative point estimate for outcome_006 but an interval crossing zero, so it remains unresolved but closed as a weaker counterpart to the H146 pattern. Overall, no claim is accepted from discovery evidence; validation of H145 is the next most useful independent test.

Research goal: investigate which measured predictors and subgroups are associated with scientifically meaningful differences in outcome_012 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_005 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_015 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_002 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_016 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_007 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_013 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_014 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_004 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_009 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_010 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_001 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_008 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_003 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_006 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_011 (CRISPR dependency score). Use the supplied dataset to discover and follow up comparisons, assess effect sizes and uncertainty, and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.

Predictor names and text categorical values use opaque labels. Levels are nominal labels, not ordered numbers. Numeric values, outcome scales, and missingness are preserved.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Your action now: Assess new validation and any response deadlines listed below. Explain what you conclude and what to investigate next. Accepted claims update automatically.

For H145, outcome_006 with feature_052 1 versus 0 in the claimed stronger-dependency direction, discovery was marginal but original-direction positive: signed estimate +0.0412, interval [0.0008, 0.0816], using the approximate 10%-of-absolute-mean benchmark near 0.0093. Independent validation, however, reversed and was essentially null: signed estimate -0.0051, interval [-0.0658, 0.0556]. Because the independent point estimate is not clinically meaningful, the sign is opposite, and the interval includes both no effect and subthreshold effects, I reject H145 and close it. This failure is consistent with the broader pattern in this dataset: several discovery-significant or near-threshold associations for feature_052, feature_060, feature_008, feature_047, feature_009, feature_023, and related predictor families have not replicated independently.

For H24, outcome_011 with feature_027 1 versus 0 in the claimed stronger-dependency direction, discovery was already subthreshold and null: signed estimate +0.0070, interval [-0.0231, 0.0371]. Validation is also null and essentially zero: signed estimate -0.0002, interval [-0.0391, 0.0388]. I reject H24 and close it. For the response-deadline claims, H79 and H1 both remain rejected. H79, outcome_001 feature_009 level_001 versus level_003 in the negative-dependency direction, had a clinically sized discovery result signed to that direction (R54: +0.0808 [0.0166, 0.1449]), but independent validation reversed and was null (R76: -0.0319 [-0.1149, 0.0510]). H1, outcome_001 feature_002 1 versus 0, was null at discovery and validation is subthreshold and imprecise (R77: +0.0354 [-0.0118, 0.0826], below the approximate 0.0415 benchmark for outcome_001). Thus the feature_002, feature_009 rare-level, feature_034, feature_008/feature_047, feature_023, and feature_052 families remain unsupported after discovery or validation.

The only scientifically informative unresolved pattern is the reversed feature_063 signal on outcome_014. The originally registered stronger-dependency claim H146 was rejected because its signed interval was entirely negative. The corresponding reversed claim H148 is supported by R101: feature_063 level_002 versus level_001 has a positive raw mean_difference, signed for direction +1 as +0.0361 [0.0022, 0.0701]. For outcome_014, with absolute mean about 0.093, the point estimate is roughly 39% of the absolute mean, but the lower bound is far below the 10% clinical benchmark. Because this is a discovery-only result from a multiplicity-heavy search and its interval permits clinically subthreshold effects, I do not accept H148. I keep it active as a focused follow-up target. The proposed follow-up is to test the same feature_063 contrast on outcome_006 in the corresponding reversed direction, and to probe level_003 versus level_001 to assess whether the pattern is robust and possibly dose-related across adjacent dependency outcomes.

Overall scientific conclusion: no association in this dataset has met the threshold for acceptance when effect size, uncertainty, multiplicity, and available validation are considered. Major negative or non-reproducible findings include feature_002/outcome_001, feature_009 rare levels for outcome_001 and outcome_007, feature_008/feature_047 for outcome_008, feature_023 for outcome_001, feature_052 for outcome_006, and feature_027 for outcome_011. The best remaining uncertainty is whether feature_063 level_002 relative to level_001 marks weaker dependency on outcome_014, possibly extending to outcome_006. The next most informative analysis is to test the proposed reversed feature_063 outcome_006 comparison and related feature_063 level contrasts, then request independent validation only if a coherent multi-outcome or dose-consistent pattern emerges. All conclusions remain dataset-specific associations and do not establish causality or generalizability.

Research goal: investigate which measured predictors and subgroups are associated with scientifically meaningful differences in outcome_012 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_005 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_015 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_002 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_016 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_007 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_013 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_014 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_004 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_009 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_010 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_001 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_008 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_003 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_006 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_011 (CRISPR dependency score). Use the supplied dataset to discover and follow up comparisons, assess effect sizes and uncertainty, and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.

Predictor names and text categorical values use opaque labels. Levels are nominal labels, not ordered numbers. Numeric values, outcome scales, and missingness are preserved.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Your action now: Propose scientifically useful new comparisons or refinements for later analysis.

record.narrative:
No assessments are due. The main residual scientific question is whether feature_063 is a real dependency-score predictor, especially for the near-zero outcomes outcome_014 and outcome_006. The reversed feature_063 pattern is not accepted yet: for outcome_014, level_002 versus level_001 has raw positive mean_difference, signed for direction +1 as +0.0361 [0.0022, 0.0701] (R101), but the lower bound is below the approximate 10%-of-absolute-mean benchmark of about 0.0093. For outcome_006, the same contrast has a positive point estimate +0.0218 [-0.0126, 0.0563] (R102), but it is imprecise. This paired same-sign pattern is hypothesis-generating, not accepted, because discovery was heavily multiplicity-prone and independent validation has already falsified several earlier marginal leads.

I therefore registered focused refinements rather than accepting H148 or H149. First, I added feature_063 level_003 versus level_002 for outcome_014 and outcome_006. Together with the already registered level_003 versus level_001 comparisons, these will clarify whether non-reference levels move in the same candidate weaker-dependency direction, whether only level_002 differs, or whether the pattern is non-monotonic/nominal. Second, I added the key level_002 versus level_001 contrast within the high-prevalence feature_008=1 eligibility stratum. feature_008-related leads failed independent validation, so persistence of the feature_063 contrast in this large stratum would be more credible than a full-population association that could be diluted by collinear or high-prevalence markers. Attenuation would suggest dependence on that marker family and would argue against acceptance. Third, I extended feature_063 level_003 versus level_001 to outcome_008 and outcome_011 to test whether the candidate effect is limited to the near-zero outcome pair or is broader.

I also registered paired high-count categorical screens for feature_019, feature_036, and feature_055 on outcome_014 and outcome_006. These predictors have adequate known cell counts and are less saturated than the previously tested high-prevalence binary families. I framed all positive claims in the direction of higher/less-negative dependency score, i.e. weaker dependency, because that is the direction of the existing feature_063 signal; the anticipated direction is uncertain for the new predictors. A single positive screen should not be accepted. For these small-threshold near-zero outcomes, I will require a clinically meaningful point estimate, cross-outcome consistency, and preferably a validation or at least a decisive interval before acceptance.

Current decision rule: if feature_063 gives a coherent positive pattern across levels/outcomes, with at least one clinically decisive result whose lower bound exceeds the relevant benchmark, I will consider validation. If the pattern remains only H148 with an interval permitting subthreshold effects, or if stratum restriction attenuates it, I will reject. The new categorical screens require the same evidence discipline. All proposed effects remain dataset-specific associations and do not establish causality or generalizability.

record.narrative:
None of the newly delivered discovery comparisons is acceptable from discovery evidence alone. All estimates are already signed to the registered hypothesis direction; positive signed estimates for feature_063 mean exposed-minus-comparator raw evidence for higher, less negative dependency scores, i.e. weaker dependency, while negative signed estimates mean the opposite raw direction. Approximate 10%-of-absolute-mean clinical benchmarks are about 0.0093 for outcome_014/outcome_006, 0.028 for outcome_008, and 0.030 for outcome_011.

The feature_063 battery is still only hypothesis-generating. H150 and H151 show large positive point estimates for level_003 versus level_001 on outcome_014 (+0.0576) and outcome_006 (+0.0617), but their intervals are wide and include both no effect and clinically opposite effects. H152 and H153 are positive for level_003 versus level_002, which is nominally consistent with a nondecreasing level pattern, but level_003 has only 98 exposed observations and the intervals are too imprecise to infer dose-response. H154 and H155 remain positive within the high-prevalence feature_008=1 stratum, which argues against simple attenuation in that stratum, but their lower bounds cross zero and therefore are not clinically or statistically decisive. By contrast, H134 is small and opposite on outcome_008, H135 is null on outcome_011, and H156/H157 do not support extending the candidate effect beyond outcome_014/outcome_006. Thus I close the cross-outcome feature_063 checks H134, H135, H156, and H157, keep the paired outcome_014/outcome_006 level_003 checks active as context, and defer the more fragile dose and stratum probes.

The feature_036 screens are not compelling: H160 and H161 have negative point estimates against the claimed weaker-dependency direction, with intervals crossing zero. They do not justify acceptance or a refinement now. The only currently strong candidate remains H148, outcome_014 feature_063 level_002 versus level_001: signed estimate +0.0361 [0.0022, 0.0701]. It is the only feature_063 interval in this family that excludes zero, and the new battery makes it more plausible as an outcome_014/outcome_006-centered association rather than a broad dependency-score predictor. However, its lower bound is far below the clinical benchmark, it comes from a heavily multiplicity-prone discovery search, and independent validation has falsified many earlier near-threshold leads. Therefore I do not accept it yet, but I request independent validation of H148 because it is the most informative single test of the remaining candidate. If validation is null, opposite, or lower-bound dominated, the feature_063 family should be closed. If validation supports it, I will reassess H148, H149, H150/H151, and H154/H155 before considering any broader claim. These remain dataset-specific associations, not causal or generalizable claims.

Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.

Predictor names and text categorical values use opaque labels. Levels are nominal labels, not ordered numbers. Numeric values, outcome scales, and missingness are preserved.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Your action now: Assess new validation and any response deadlines listed below. Explain what you conclude and what to investigate next. Accepted claims update automatically.

record.narrative:
The newly delivered validation evidence resolves one candidate lead and leaves the remaining feature_063 signal scientifically ambiguous rather than clinically established. For H89 (outcome_008, feature_008 1 vs 0, claimed stronger dependency), discovery R73 was nominally supportive: signed estimate +0.0322, interval [0.0028, 0.0617]. However, its lower bound was well below the outcome_008 clinical benchmark (about 0.028), and independent validation R90 was not supportive: signed estimate -0.0033, interval [-0.0500, 0.0434]. The validation point estimate is negligible, the sign is opposite to the claimed direction, and the interval includes no effect, clinically meaningful effects in either direction, and imprecision that cannot support a clinically significant difference. Therefore H89 is rejected and closed. This is another non-replication of a discovery-only marginal association in the feature_008/feature_047-related high-prevalence binary family.

For H148 (outcome_014, feature_063 level_002 vs level_001, direction +1, meaning a raw higher, less-negative dependency score in exposed relative to comparator), the evidence is more nuanced. Discovery R101 gave signed estimate +0.0361, interval [0.0022, 0.0701], so the point estimate is clinically sizable relative to the outcome_014 absolute-mean benchmark of roughly 0.0093, but the lower bound allows clinically subthreshold effects and only barely excludes zero. Independent validation R117 is same-sign but imprecise: signed estimate +0.0234, interval [-0.0271, 0.0740]. The point estimate again exceeds the approximate 10% benchmark, but the validation interval includes zero and clinically subthreshold values, and these independent intervals are conservative because they account for the validation budget and the large number of validation comparisons in the run. Taken together, the two estimates favor the proposed direction, but they do not establish a scientifically meaningful difference with adequate precision. Therefore I do not accept H148; I keep it unresolved. It remains the best remaining dataset-specific uncertainty because it is the only feature_063 contrast with discovery evidence excluding zero, and the independent validation was not opposed, but its uncertainty is too large to license an accepted claim.

The surrounding feature_063 evidence does not strengthen the claim enough to change that judgment. H149 (outcome_006, same contrast, signed positive direction) is directionally consistent but not decisive: discovery R102 is +0.0218, interval [-0.0126, 0.0563], with both lower and upper bounds permitting no effect or subthreshold effects. The level_003 versus level_001 and level_003 versus level_002 checks for outcome_014/outcome_006 have positive point estimates but very wide intervals because level_003 has only 98 observations, so they cannot establish dose-response. The stratum checks within feature_008=1 remain positive but are also not decisive. Cross-outcome checks for outcome_008 and outcome_011 do not support extension beyond the near-zero outcome_014/outcome_006 pair. Thus the feature_063 family remains dataset-specific and unaccepted.

The broader scientific conclusion for the current evidence base is unchanged: no association has yet met the combined threshold of clinically meaningful effect size, sufficient precision, multiplicity control, and independent validation. The new H89 validation adds a negative finding. H148 remains the principal unresolved lead, but it should not be described as a supported predictor-subgroup association. All conclusions remain associations within the supplied dataset and do not establish causality or generalizability.

The most informative next analysis is to test whether the H148 signal is coherent in the paired near-zero outcome outcome_006 and in a prespecified clinical-feature subgroup. I registered mean-difference refinements for outcome_014 and outcome_006, feature_063 level_002 versus level_001 within feature_024 >= -7.353, the observed median split of this numeric clinical feature, plus an interaction refinement for outcome_014. If feature_063 shows a coherent clinically meaningful pattern in these targeted subgroup comparisons or if H149 gains clinically decisive evidence, H148 and H149 could be revisited together. If these focused subgroup analyses remain imprecise or attenuate the effect, the feature_063 family should be closed without further validation.

record.narrative:
No assessments are due, so this stage adds focused refinements rather than reassessments. The main residual hypothesis-generating signal is the feature_063 level_002 versus level_001 pattern for the near-zero outcomes outcome_014 and outcome_006. Because these claims are direction +1, positive signed estimates correspond to a raw exposed-minus-comparator increase, i.e. less-negative dependency scores or weaker dependency. H148 is still the strongest feature_063 claim: discovery R101 +0.0361 [0.0022, 0.0701], validation R117 +0.0234 [-0.0271, 0.0740]. The signs agree and point estimates are above the approximate absolute-mean benchmark for outcome_014, but the uncertainty still permits clinically subthreshold or null effects. I therefore add targeted clinical-feature subgroup tests rather than accepting the broad claim. H164/H165 test the level_002 versus level_001 contrast in the feature_024 >= -7.353 stratum, and H166 tests whether the effect is larger in that stratum for outcome_014. I add the paired outcome_006 interaction and the feature_024 <= -7.353 complement mean differences to determine whether the candidate effect is concentrated above or below the median clinical-feature value, is roughly equal across strata, or attenuates in both. The expected raw direction remains positive for feature_063 level_002 versus level_001 in both strata under the residual weaker-dependency hypothesis, but I keep anticipated_direction uncertain for new strata/interactions because the observed pattern could be false positive, stratum-limited, or opposite. A clinically decisive decision requires same-sign cross-outcome consistency, point estimates exceeding the outcome-specific 10% absolute-mean benchmark, and intervals that are not dominated by no-effect or subthreshold values.

I also register a focused follow-up for the unresolved outcome_001 feature_023 lead. R66 showed raw positive mean_difference +0.0514 [-0.0024, 0.1052] for feature_023=1 versus 0, which is clinically sizable relative to outcome_001 mean magnitude but still imprecise. Because feature_023 is highly prevalent and outcome_001 has a larger absolute mean, median splitting of feature_024 may identify whether the lead is diluted across the full population or concentrated in one clinical-feature stratum. The explicit hypothesis is that feature_023=1 is associated with weaker dependency (less-negative outcome_001) within one or both median strata; alternatives are no association, stronger dependency, or an effect confined to one stratum. I also test the corresponding interaction to assess whether feature_024 modifies the feature_023 contrast. Finally, I test outcome_001 feature_063 level_002 versus level_001 as a specificity check: if the feature_063 association is broad, it should also appear clinically meaningfully on outcome_001; if it is confined to the near-zero outcome_014/outcome_006 pair, this comparison should be null, small, or opposite. All proposals remain dataset-specific association tests and do not establish causality or generalizability.

Iteration 10/25, stage analyze, attempt 1.
