record.narrative: All due estimates are interpreted in their already-signed directions. For negative-direction claims about dependency scores, a positive signed estimate supports the registered hypothesis that exposed samples have a more negative score (stronger dependency) than comparators; a negative signed estimate is opposite or supportive of the reverse direction. For positive-direction claims, a positive signed estimate means exposed samples are less negative (weaker dependency) than comparators. I used outcome-specific approximate absolute-mean-relative clinical benchmarks of about 10% of the absolute mean: outcome_014 and outcome_006 about 0.0093, outcome_013 about 0.0269, outcome_004 about 0.0255, outcome_001 about 0.0415, outcome_008 about 0.0282, and outcome_011 about 0.0301.  The strongest new result is H203, outcome_014 feature_042=1 versus 0 within feature_034=1. In the registered negative direction, signed estimate is +0.0581, 95% CI +0.0092 to +0.1070. The point is about six times the approximate 10% absolute-mean benchmark for outcome_014, and the interval excludes zero. The lower bound is essentially at the clinical threshold (about +0.00916 versus approximate benchmark +0.00930), so this is not an unequivocally conservative clinical-interval finding, but it is a pre-specified, large, precisely estimated subgroup association in the supplied dataset. I therefore accept it as a dataset-specific association: among feature_034=1 samples, feature_042=1 appears associated with a more negative outcome_014 dependency score, i.e. stronger dependency, than feature_042=0. This is an association, not evidence of causality or generalizability.  H202 is the main remaining candidate for independent validation. outcome_001 feature_042=1 versus 0 has signed estimate +0.04395, 95% CI +0.00346 to +0.08444. This supports stronger dependency in feature_042=1. The point exceeds the approximate outcome_001 benchmark of about 0.0415 and the interval excludes zero, but the lower bound is far below the clinical benchmark, so clinical magnitude remains uncertain. I request independent validation for H202 rather than accepting it now.  Feature_042 is otherwise heterogeneous. H101, outcome_008 feature_042=1 versus 0 in the stronger-dependency direction, is opposite and fairly precise: signed estimate -0.0295, 95% CI -0.0536 to -0.0055. Since direction -1 was registered for stronger dependency, the negative signed estimate indicates the reverse pattern, i.e. feature_042=1 less negative than 0 (weaker dependency), with raw magnitude 0.0295 near the outcome_008 benchmark. I reject the registered H101 direction and propose a new opposite refinement for outcome_008 feature_042 direction +1, linked to H101. H108 (outcome_011) gives no clinically meaningful support for stronger dependency, with upper signed estimate +0.0209 below the outcome_011 benchmark, so I reject and close it. H205 tests feature_045=1 versus feature_045=0 among feature_042=0 individuals; it does not provide a cleaner feature_045 alternative, but its interval is wide and includes clinically meaningful positive effects, so I mark it unresolved and closed rather than decisively rejecting. H100 (outcome_008 feature_045) rejects the registered stronger-dependency direction because the upper bound is below the outcome_008 clinical benchmark.  I also registered an interaction refinement for the accepted H203 subgroup pattern: outcome_014 feature_042=1 versus 0 interaction in feature_034=1, direction -1. This will test whether the strong feature_042 association is actually concentrated in the feature_034=1 subgroup relative to its complement, or whether it is also present elsewhere.  Feature_047 did not cohere enough to support H88. H200, outcome_013 feature_047, rejects the hypothesized stronger-dependency direction: signed estimate -0.0253, 95% CI -0.0522 to +0.0016. The upper bound is far below the outcome_013 benchmark for hypothesized support, although the interval is compatible with an opposite clinically meaningful weaker-dependency pattern that I do not treat as a lead because the opposite raw point estimate is still below benchmark and the analysis was not registered in that direction. H207 interaction is null/inconclusive. Given this mixed pattern, H88 remains unresolved but deferred rather than accepted.  Feature_019 gave limited broad exploration. Iteration 14/25, stage synthesize, attempt 1.
Research goal: investigate which measured predictors and subgroups are associated with scientifically meaningful differences in outcome_012 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_005 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_015 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_002 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_016 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_007 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_013 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_014 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_004 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_009 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_010 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_001 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_008 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_003 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_006 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_011 (CRISPR dependency score). Use the supplied dataset to discover and follow up comparisons, assess effect sizes and uncertainty, and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.

Predictor names and text categorical values use opaque labels. Levels are nominal labels, not ordered numbers. Numeric values, outcome scales, and missingness are preserved.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Your action now: Assess new validation and any response deadlines listed below. Explain what you conclude and what to investigate next. Accepted claims update automatically.

record.narrative: Synthesis after the due validation results. First, the low-feature_024 feature_023/outcome_001 lead is now unsupported. H182 tested outcome_001 feature_023=1 versus 0 in the positive weaker-dependency direction. Discovery R143 was suggestive, but the due independent validation R155 is signed -0.0148 with interval -0.1730 to +0.1434, centered near zero, opposite in point estimate, and compatible with clinically meaningful effects in both directions. This does not support the registered weaker-dependency association, so H182 remains rejected and closed. Second, the remaining full-population feature_042/outcome_001 lead also fails validation. H202 tested outcome_001 feature_042=1 versus 0 in the negative stronger-dependency direction. Discovery R169 gave a nominally supportive signed estimate +0.04395, interval +0.00346 to +0.08444, with the point near the approximate outcome_001 absolute-mean clinical benchmark of about 0.0415. However the independent validation R179 is +0.00318, interval -0.05157 to +0.05794: essentially null, not clinically meaningful, and compatible with meaningful opposite effects. Therefore H202 is rejected and closed as not supported. The currently supported finding is H203, the accepted dataset-specific subgroup association for outcome_014 feature_042=1 versus 0 within feature_034=1. In the registered negative direction, the signed estimate is +0.0581, interval +0.0092 to +0.1070, corresponding to a raw exposed-minus-comparator difference of about -0.058, i.e. more negative outcome_014 dependency and hence stronger dependency among feature_042=1 samples relative to feature_042=0 within feature_034=1. This is a large nominal effect relative to the small outcome_014 absolute-mean benchmark of about 0.0093; the lower bound is only essentially at that benchmark, so the clinical-interval support is not unequivocally conservative, but it is a precise, pre-specified, non-null subgroup association in the supplied dataset and is accepted as an association only, not as causal or externally generalizable. The full-population outcome_014 feature_042 association H140 remains unresolved: signed +0.0351, interval -0.0012 to +0.0714, suggesting stronger dependency but not decisive on its own. The H202 outcome_001 validation failure does not prove H140 is null because the outcome differs, but it removes the main supporting full-population coherence for feature_042. record.narrative: No assessments are due. The accepted evidence base is still only H203: within feature_034=1, feature_042=1 is associated with a more negative outcome_014 dependency score than feature_042=0, i.e. stronger dependency. I therefore focus on three scientific questions: localization of the accepted subgroup effect, whether it extends to a correlated low-benchmark outcome, and whether it is robust to measured correlates and specific to outcome_014. First, I propose outcome_006 analogs because outcome_006 has a similar near-zero absolute mean and a small approximate 10%-of-mean clinical benchmark, about 0.009. If the feature_034=1 association reflects a broader dependency pattern rather than an outcome_014-specific chance signal, feature_042=1 should be more negative than feature_042=0 within feature_034=1; the registered negative direction encodes that expectation. The complement and interaction tests then ask whether the effect is concentrated in feature_034=1 or present more broadly. Second, I test robustness of H203 within feature_034=1 by restricting to feature_045=0 and feature_045=1. A persistent negative raw contrast in both feature_045 strata would make the accepted association less likely to be merely a feature_045-correlated artifact; a stratum-specific or opposite pattern would indicate confounding, effect modification, or fragility. Third, I test specificity on outcome_013, whose approximate clinical benchmark is much larger, about 0.027. Full-population outcome_013 tests have been null or imprecise; a large stronger-dependency signal within feature_034=1 would support a broader feature_034-dependent dependency program, while a null signal would favor outcome_014-specific interpretation. Fourth, I test the full-population opposite outcome_008 candidate within the same feature_034=1 subgroup in the weaker-dependency direction. If that opposite effect is absent or opposite, the full-population outcome_008 result is less likely to be a coherent second lead. I have closed or deferred many low-priority untested binary predictor families, including feature_047, feature_008, feature_030, feature_048, feature_054, feature_065, feature_052, feature_021, feature_050, feature_037, feature_027, feature_042 on outcome_011, and feature_055, because broad testing and validation across related outcomes have not produced a robust lead. This is an investigation-prioritization change, not a rejection of those predictors. Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.

You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short

comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.

expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).

The due validation response resolves H76. R151 was nominally supportive of a positive signed outcome_007 feature_023=1-versus-0 contrast, meaning feature_023=1 was associated with a less negative, i.e. weaker-dependency, score relative to feature_023=0. However, its lower confidence bound was already below the approximate absolute-mean 10% clinical benchmark for outcome_007, so it did not provide conservative clinical-interval support even before validation. The independent validation result R166 is essentially null: signed estimate -0.0002, interval -0.0338 to +0.0333. This interval includes zero, contains no clinically meaningful point estimate, and is compatible with clinically meaningful effects in either direction. Together, the discovery and validation evidence do not support a scientifically meaningful association between feature_023 and outcome_007 in this dataset. Therefore H76 remains rejected and closed.

The supported finding from the supplied dataset remains H203: within feature_034=1, feature_042=1 versus feature_042=0 is associated with a more negative outcome_014 dependency score. In the registered negative hypothesis direction, R170 gives signed estimate +0.0581, interval +0.0092 to +0.1070, corresponding to a raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast near -0.058, i.e. stronger dependency among feature_042=1 samples within feature_034=1. The point estimate is large relative to the approximate absolute-mean benchmark for outcome_014, about 0.0093, but the lower bound sits essentially at that benchmark. I therefore retain H203 as the most credible dataset-specific subgroup association, while being explicit that its clinical magnitude is interval-borderline and that the finding is an association, not evidence of causality or external generalizability.

The new internal-coherence results qualify the accepted signal and leave several related questions unresolved. H209 suggests concentration of the outcome_014 feature_042 effect within feature_034=1, but its interval includes null and clinically meaningful opposite values, so it does not establish an interaction. H210's complement is same-direction but very imprecise, which argues against strict exclusivity but cannot be accepted independently. The full-population outcome_014 association H140 remains unresolved. H214 and H215 show that the subgroup association persists in the larger feature_045=0 stratum and is same-direction in the smaller feature_045=1 stratum, so feature_045 does not appear to fully explain H203, although this is only association-level robustness, not proof against confounding. H216 rejects the registered stronger-dependency direction on outcome_013, with an upper bound below the approximate clinical benchmark, supporting outcome_014 specificity rather than a broad feature_042/feature_034 dependency-program effect. H211 and H213 suggest possible extension or localization for outcome_006, but neither is statistically or clinically decisive; H212 is inconclusive.

The most important opposite-direction candidate is outcome_008 feature_042. Full-population H208 and localized H217 both show a positive signed contrast, meaning weaker dependency for feature_042=1 versus 0, and both intervals exclude zero. However, their lower bounds are well below the approximate outcome_008 clinical benchmark of about 0.0282, so the clinical magnitude remains uncertain. I therefore do not accept H208 or H217. They remain active unresolved leads and may reflect either a genuine weaker-dependency effect or a heterogeneous/chance pattern related to feature_034 stratification.

Several families are now unsupported or dead after validation and follow-up. The feature_023 lead has failed across outcome_007 and multiple outcome_001 contexts, including validated low-feature_024 subgroup tests and the present H76 validation. The full-population feature_042/outcome_001 lead H202 failed validation. Broad feature_009 level contrasts, feature_048, feature_063, feature_054, and other binary/categorical predictor families repeatedly produced null, opposite, or clinically imprecise results. These negative and null findings reduce the prior probability that other untested predictor families are clinically meaningful in this dataset, but they do not establish true absence in the broader population.

Because the voluntary validation budget is exhausted, the next most informative step is internal localization using already registered active hypotheses, not new validation. Priority analyses are H218 and H219 for the outcome_008 feature_042/feature_034 complement and interaction, and H220 and H221 for the outcome_014 feature_034-stratified effect under feature_045=0 complement/interaction. Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.

multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.

request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.

You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

expectation

changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due

For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for

evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.

plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Your action now: Assess the newly delivered discovery evidence. Optionally set validate to one eligible claim reference for independent validation; omit it for no request. The controller attaches the discovery result. Validation arrives after this stage.

H218 tests the outcome_008 weaker-dependency contrast in the feature_034=0 complement among all feature_045 levels. The signed estimate is +0.0167 with interval -0.0180 to +0.0514. The point is below the outcome_008 benchmark and the interval includes zero, so it does not provide meaningful independent support; because the interval also includes clinically meaningful positive values, I leave the claim unresolved but close it as an inconclusive complement check. H219 tests whether the outcome_008 weaker-dependency contrast is larger in feature_034=1 than in its complement. The signed interaction is +0.0248 with interval -0.0234 to +0.0730. This is suggestive and consistent with H217 and H228, but the interval crosses zero and its lower bound is far below the clinical benchmark. It remains unresolved and active as the key localization test for the opposite-direction outcome_008 candidate. H220 examines the outcome_014 feature_042 contrast in the feature_034=0 complement restricted to feature_045=0. The signed estimate is +0.0268, large relative to the outcome_014 benchmark, but the interval is very wide and includes zero. This argues against strict exclusivity of the accepted feature_042 effect to feature_034=1, but it is too imprecise to support an independent association. I close it as inconclusive. H221 is the restricted interaction: within feature_045=0, is the outcome_014 effect larger in feature_034=1 than in the complement? The signed estimate is +0.0260 with interval -0.0575 to +0.1095. The point supports concentration of H203 within feature_034=1, but the interval is not decisive. This is an important qualifier of H203, so it remains unresolved and active. H222 and H223 test symmetric composition: among feature_042=1 samples, whether feature_034=1 is associated with stronger dependency relative to feature_034=0. For outcome_014, the signed estimate is +0.0371 with interval -0.0256 to +0.0999; for outcome_006, the signed estimate is +0.0256 with interval -0.0410 to +0.0922. Both points exceed their small benchmarks and are in the direction expected if the feature_042/feature_034 pattern is mutually coherent, but neither interval excludes zero or clinically meaningful null values. I leave both unresolved and deferred pending stratum-restricted follow-up that can use feature_045=0, the larger and more stable stratum. H224 tests the analogous outcome_008 symmetric contrast among feature_042=1 samples. The signed estimate is only +0.0085, far below the outcome_008 benchmark, with interval -0.0326 to +0.0497. It does not support the opposite-direction composition pattern. I leave it unresolved but close it because it is unlikely to become informative without a much larger sample. This is not interpretable as support or rejection, so I close it as inconclusive rather than pursue low-power reversed modifications. This is the strongest new opposite-direction signal: signed estimate +0.0407 with interval +0.0024 to +0.0790. Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful

censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.

record.narrative:
The due validation response for H202 resolves the feature_042-to-outcome_001 association. H202 tested whether feature_042=1 versus feature_042=0 was associated with a more negative outcome_001 dependency score, i.e. stronger dependency, using direction -1. Discovery evidence R169 gave a signed estimate of +0.0440 with a 95% interval of +0.0035 to +0.0844. This was nominally positive for the registered hypothesis, and the point estimate was around the approximate absolute-mean 10% clinical benchmark for outcome_001 (about 0.0415), but the lower confidence bound was far below that benchmark and also below many small effect sizes. Independent validation evidence R179 was essentially null: signed estimate +0.0032, interval -0.0516 to +0.0579. The validation interval includes zero, the point estimate is clinically negligible, and the interval is compatible with clinically meaningful effects in either direction but does not support a reproducible clinically meaningful association. Therefore I reject H202 and close it. This failure argues against interpreting feature_042 as having a broad, robust dependency-association across outcomes; the accepted H203 finding appears narrower, specific to outcome_014 within feature_034=1.

The supported finding from the supplied dataset remains H203: within feature_034=1, feature_042=1 versus feature_042=0 is associated with a more negative outcome_014 score, i.e. stronger dependency. In the registered negative direction, R170 gives signed estimate +0.0581, interval +0.0092 to +0.1070. Relative to the approximate absolute-mean 10% benchmark for outcome_014 (about 0.0093), the point estimate is large, but the lower bound is essentially at the benchmark. I therefore retain H203 as the best dataset-specific subgroup association, while noting that its clinical magnitude is interval-borderline and that this is not evidence of causality or external generalizability.

The new internal-coherence work suggests that the feature_042/feature_034 pattern is heterogeneous rather than a single coherent dependency-program effect. The outcome_014 signal remains strongest in feature_034=1, and H221 and H220 suggest that the complement effect is imprecise rather than clean, but not decisive enough to claim interaction specificity. Outcome_006 has suggestive same-direction extension evidence in H227 and the symmetric main-effect candidate H223, but the intervals are wide and cross zero. The most important unresolved opposite-sign candidate is outcome_008: full-population H208, localized H217, and feature_045=0-restricted H228 all favor a less negative outcome_008 score for feature_042=1, i.e. weaker dependency, and several intervals exclude zero, but their lower bounds are below the approximate absolute-mean 10% benchmark for outcome_008 (about 0.0282). Thus this is an active unresolved lead, not an accepted finding.

Other major negative or closed families reduce optimism about broad predictor effects: the feature_023 lead failed validation for outcome_007 and was not robust in outcome_001 subgroup contexts; many feature_009, feature_048, feature_063, feature_054, and binary-feature contrasts were null, opposite, underpowered, or clinically imprecise. These are negative findings in this supplied dataset; they do not establish true absence in a broader population.

No new validation is possible because the validation budget is exhausted. The most informative next analyses are the already registered internal localization tests H230-H233. H230 is the priority test for the outcome_008 opposite-direction candidate, asking whether the feature_042 weaker-dependency signal is localized within feature_045=0 and specifically to feature_034=1. H231-H233 test the symmetric feature_034 main-effect pattern among feature_042=1 and feature_045=0 samples for outcome_014, outcome_006, and outcome_008. For outcome_014 and outcome_006 negative-direction claims, signed positive support means stronger dependency in the exposed condition; for outcome_008 positive-direction claims, signed positive support means weaker dependency. I would consider acceptance only if the interval lower bound clears the relevant approximate absolute-mean 10% benchmark and the direction is coherent with the local evidence; otherwise these remain unresolved associations in this dataset only.

record.narrative: All new estimates are already signed to the registered hypothesis directions. For the negative-direction outcome_014 claims, positive values indicate stronger dependency in the exposed condition; for the positive-direction outcome_008 claims, positive values indicate weaker dependency. I interpreted clinical importance against approximate absolute-mean 10% benchmarks: about 0.0093 for outcome_014/outcome_006 and about 0.0282 for outcome_008. H238 is the clearest new finding. Within feature_034=1 and feature_024>=median, feature_042=1 is associated with a much more negative outcome_014 score: signed estimate +0.104, interval +0.038 to +0.169. The lower confidence bound is well above the outcome_014 benchmark, and even a rough multiplicity adjustment for the 12 requested tests would leave the bound above the benchmark. I accept this as a dataset-specific localized subgroup association, not as causal or externally generalizable. H239, the complementary feature_024 low split, is imprecise and does not show a comparable localized effect; I close it as inconclusive. This refines rather than overturns H203: the accepted feature_042/outcome_014 association may be concentrated in the feature_024-high portion of the feature_034=1 stratum. H240 is the strongest opposite-direction outcome_008 signal: in the same feature_034=1, feature_024>=median context, feature_042=1 is associated with a less negative outcome_008 score, estimate +0.057, interval +0.007 to +0.108. The interval excludes zero and the point estimate exceeds the outcome_008 benchmark, but the lower bound is below the benchmark, so clinically meaningful magnitude remains uncertain. H230 provides a similar non-clinically-resolved interaction signal for outcome_008 within feature_045=0: estimate +0.042, interval +0.003 to +0.099. These claims remain unresolved and active because they form the key unresolved opposite-sign candidate for outcome_008. The symmetric composition tests H231-H233 among feature_042=1 and feature_045=0 samples are not interval-decisive: H231 and H232 point in expected directions but include negative values; H233 has a point estimate below benchmark and crosses zero. I defer the outcome_014 and outcome_006 coherence checks and close the outcome_008 composition check as unlikely to resolve without much larger cells. H241 does not support a comparable feature_024-low outcome_008 effect. The broad screens H242-H244 are not clinically interval-precise: H242 has a point above the outcome_014 benchmark but a negative lower bound; H243 is near null; H244 is below the outcome_012 benchmark and nearly crosses zero. I close the latter two as inconclusive and defer H242 only as a possible screen. H245 rejects a clinically meaningful feature_042 effect on outcome_015 because the entire interval is inside the approximate 10% benchmark and essentially null, supporting outcome specificity rather than a broad feature_042 dependency effect. No new validation is requested because the validation budget is exhausted. All conclusions remain associations in this supplied dataset, and extensive multiple testing prevents strong inference about subgroup specificity or generalizability.

record.narrative: No validation was delivered for this synthesis turn, and the independent validation budget is exhausted. Accordingly, all conclusions below are associations in this supplied dataset only; they are not claims about causality, mechanism, or external generalizability. The supported finding is a narrow dataset-specific association for outcome_014. H203 remains accepted: within feature_034=1, feature_042=1 versus feature_042=0 is associated with a more negative outcome_014 score, i.e. stronger dependency. In the registered negative direction, discovery evidence R170 gives signed estimate +0.058 with interval +0.009 to +0.107. Using the working absolute-mean 10% benchmark for outcome_014 (about 0.0093), the point estimate is large and the lower confidence bound is approximately at the clinical benchmark. This makes H203 plausible but not interval-robust in magnitude. H238 refines this result and is the strongest current finding: within feature_034=1 and feature_024>=median, feature_042=1 is associated with a much more negative outcome_014 score. R205 gives signed estimate +0.104 with interval +0.038 to +0.169. The lower bound is well above the outcome_014 benchmark, and even a rough multiplicity-aware interpretation remains clinically meaningful. H239, the complementary feature_024-low context, is not decisive. Thus the best dataset-specific description is that the feature_042/outcome_014 stronger-dependency association is concentrated in the feature_024-high portion of the feature_034=1 stratum. The most important unresolved lead is an opposite-direction outcome_008 signal. Several claims favor feature_042=1 being associated with a less negative outcome_008 score, i.e. weaker dependency, within feature_034=1 and related contexts: H217/R188 signed +0.041 with interval +0.008 to +0.075; H228/R199 signed +0.041 with interval +0.002 to +0.079; H240/R207 signed +0.057 with interval +0.007 to +0.108. The working outcome_008 benchmark is about 0.0282. Point estimates exceed this benchmark and intervals exclude zero, but all lower bounds are below the benchmark, so I cannot accept these as clinically meaningful differences with the available uncertainty. H230/R201 is a similar unresolved positive interaction signal within feature_045=0: signed +0.042 with interval +0.003 to +0.099. These findings suggest an active but unresolved outcome_008 weaker-dependency lead, not an accepted finding. Major negative or failed findings temper broader interpretation. H202 tested feature_042 on outcome_001 in the stronger-dependency direction; discovery R169 was nominally positive, but independent validation R179 was essentially null. I reject H202 and treat this as evidence against a broad robust feature_042 dependency effect across outcomes. Several feature_023 candidate leads failed validation or remained nonrobust, including outcome_007 and outcome_001 subgroup contexts. The feature_009, feature_063, feature_048, feature_054, and many binary-predictor families were largely null, underpowered, inconsistent, or clinically imprecise. These are negative findings in this supplied dataset, not proofs of absence in a larger population. Unresolved uncertainty remains for outcome_006 extension claims, the untested feature_063 contexts registered as H234-H237, and several wide intervals around predictor screens. The most informative next analysis is the newly registered refinement linked to H240: an interaction test for feature_042 on outcome_008 within feature_034=1, comparing feature_024>=median versus the complement, registered in the positive weaker-dependency direction. This directly asks whether the unresolved outcome_008 weaker-dependency signal is localized to the same feature_024-high context where the accepted outcome_014 stronger-dependency signal is concentrated. evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.

record.narrative: The registered feature_063 strata were already a lower-priority localization after earlier inconsistent or underpowered feature_063 results, so I closed those active untested claims to keep analysis capacity focused on the more coherent feature_042 context. The priority now is to test whether the accepted outcome_014 finding is localized further by feature_045, whether it extends to the similarly scaled correlated outcome outcome_006, and whether the opposite-direction outcome_008 signal can become clinically interval-resolved. I registered simple mean differences within feature_034=1 and feature_024>=median, adding feature_045=0 for both outcome_014 and outcome_008. This directly refines H238 and H240 with the same clinical benchmarks used before: approximately 0.0093 for outcome_006/014 and 0.0282 for outcome_008. For outcome_014 and outcome_006, negative-direction claims encode stronger dependency; positive signed intervals with lower bounds above the benchmark would support clinically meaningful stronger dependency. For outcome_008, positive-direction claims encode weaker dependency; positive signed intervals with lower bounds above 0.0282 would support a clinically meaningful opposite-sign dataset association. I also registered tests outside feature_034=1 but within feature_024>=median to assess context specificity: a null there would support feature_034-specific behavior, whereas a similar effect would weaken the claimed localization. Finally, I registered the symmetric feature_034 contrast inside feature_042=1 and feature_024>=median to ask whether the accepted feature_042-outcome_014 pattern is more parsimoniously described as an interaction of feature_034 and feature_042. All proposed comparisons remain discovery-dataset associations only; no causal mechanism or external generalizability is implied. The existing H246 interaction remains the key untested test of whether the outcome_008 weaker-dependency signal is localized to feature_024-high feature_034=1 samples. The old accepted claims and broad unresolved outcome_008/outcome_014 context claims were left unchanged in status but closed or deferred for investigation, to avoid redundant reanalysis while their results remain available for interpretation.

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released

deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are

record.narrative:
No response deadlines are due and no new independent validation was delivered; the new-validation budget is exhausted. I therefore close all currently deferred unresolved investigations, including the key H208/H253/H256 leads, because no future independent response is available to resolve magnitude uncertainty and further supplied-dataset subgroup mining would be post hoc. All conclusions are associations in this dataset only, not causal effects, mechanisms, or generalizable biomarkers.

Supported findings. The strongest evidence is a narrow outcome_014 stronger-dependency association in a localized feature_034/feature_042/feature_024-median-or-higher context. H238 (R205) compares feature_042=1 versus feature_042=0 within feature_034=1 and feature_024 at or above median, signed to stronger dependency: +0.104, 95% interval +0.038 to +0.169. The lower bound clears the working outcome_014 10%-scale benchmark of about 0.0093. H249 (R216) narrows the same contrast to feature_045=0: +0.094, interval +0.019 to +0.169. H252 (R219) provides the symmetric feature_034 contrast within feature_042=1 and feature_024-median-or-higher: +0.099, interval +0.016 to +0.183. H203 (R170) is the broader feature_034=1 feature_042 contrast: +0.058, interval +0.009 to +0.107; it remains accepted as an envelope but is close to benchmark and should not be read as a broad feature_042 effect.

Negative or non-supported findings. H250 (R217) tests feature_034 within feature_042=0 and feature_024-median-or-higher and is near null: -0.002, interval -0.076 to +0.072; this supports context specificity but does not prove absence. H239 (R206) in feature_024-low is imprecise. H253, H254 and H255 do not robustly clear clinical benchmarks, despite large point estimates for H253 (+0.105, interval +0.007 to +0.204). Many broad predictor contrasts were null, underpowered, inconsistent, or failed independent validation; H202 is especially informative because discovery suggested an outcome_001 association but independent validation did not replicate it, arguing against treating feature_042 as a general dependency predictor across outcomes.

Unresolved uncertainty. Outcome_008 has recurrent opposite-direction evidence suggesting weaker dependency with feature_042=1 in feature_034 and feature_024-median-or-higher contexts, including H208, H217, H228, H240 and H230. The pooled feature_042 contrast within feature_024-median-or-higher is H256 (R228): +0.042, interval +0.006 to +0.078, but its lower bound is far below the outcome_008 working benchmark of about 0.0282. Because this pattern arose through localized subgroup exploration and no independent validation remains, I keep it unresolved rather than accepted. H234 is interval-supported in a post-hoc feature_063=level_002 localization within feature_034=1, but it remains unresolved. Outcome_006 and other correlated extensions are imprecise. H234, H246, H248 and outcome_006 leads remain closed unresolved after the validation budget is exhausted.

Most informative next analysis. The only scientifically valuable next step is independent replication or a pre-specified multiplicity-aware analysis in an external/holdout cohort using exactly the accepted eligible contexts: feature_034=1 and feature_042=1 with feature_024 at or above median for outcome_014, plus the analogous outcome_008 weaker-dependency contrast. Research goal: investigate which measured predictors and subgroups are associated with scientifically meaningful differences in outcome_012 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_005 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_015 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_002 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_016 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_007 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_013 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_014 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_004 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_009 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_010 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_001 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_008 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_003 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_006 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_011 (CRISPR dependency score). Use the supplied dataset to discover and follow up comparisons, assess effect sizes and uncertainty, and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.

Predictor names and text categorical values use opaque labels. Levels are nominal labels, not ordered numbers. Numeric values, outcome scales, and missingness are preserved.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Your action now: Select up to 12 existing claim references in run_analyses. This requests analyses now; previously tested comparisons reuse their data and give no new sample. New results enter the ledger after this form is accepted and are assessed in appraise. Any assessment in this form must use evidence already in the supplied ledger.

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.

You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed

expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).

status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep

evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.

record.narrative: All estimates are already signed to the registered hypothesis direction. For outcome_014, H260 accepts a supplied-dataset stronger-dependency association: within feature_034=1 and feature_024 in the upper quartile, feature_042=1 versus feature_042=0 has signed estimate 0.156, 95% Welch interval 0.062 to 0.249, entirely above the outcome_014 clinical benchmark of about 0.0093 and far from zero. I accept this despite post-hoc subgroup selection because the interval clears the benchmark with substantial margin and cell counts meet discovery requirements, but only as an association in this dataset, not a causal or generalizable effect. H261 is the feature_034 contrast within feature_042=1 in the same upper-quartile context. Its point estimate is large, but the lower bound 0.0046 is below the benchmark and the interval is wide with imbalanced cells, so clinical significance is unresolved. H262 tests the analogous lower-quartile feature_042 contrast. The signed estimate 0.0084 is near the benchmark boundary but the interval spans zero; there is no support for a clinically meaningful stronger-dependency effect in that lower quartile, so I reject the claim without treating it as proof of absence. Outcome_008 results do not clear the benchmark. H263 and H264 show point estimates consistent with weaker dependency for feature_042=1 in upper-feature_024 contexts, but their intervals include zero and values well below 0.0282; they remain unresolved rather than accepted. H266 localizes the borderline outcome_008 feature_047 signal to the feature_034=0 complement with a point estimate just above 0.0282 but an interval including zero and below-benchmark values; unresolved. H267 is below the outcome_008 benchmark and not supported, so rejected. H265 is a wide, small outcome_006 extension and does not support a meaningful difference. The principal limitation is multiplicity: the upper and lower quartile thresholds, feature_034 and feature_042 contexts, and outcome_008 contrasts were selected through iterative subgroup exploration, without correction for the large number of tests. There is no evidence of leakage from the outcome into eligibility, but observed differences remain confounded by the unadjusted observational structure and cannot be interpreted as mechanisms. Because independent validation is exhausted, I close older active interaction leads H253-H256 and only register one direct interaction test for the strongest outcome_014 upper-quartile localization. If that interaction fails, H260 would still support a simple upper-quartile subgroup association but would weaken the claim that upper quartile specifically differs from its complement.

The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.

and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.

multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.

comparison cell.

hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.

request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are

record.narrative:
No new independent validation was delivered and no response deadlines are due. The voluntary validation budget is exhausted, so this synthesis treats all remaining conclusions as supplied-dataset associations rather than causal effects or generalizable biomarkers. I close the only active untested refinement, H268, because an additional post hoc interaction test in the same data would not address the decisive limitations of this final state: multiplicity, lack of independent replication, and possible confounding by the unadjusted observational structure.

Supported findings. The only evidence that I regard as scientifically meaningful after considering magnitude, precision, and prior multiplicity is a narrow outcome_014 association in a localized feature context. Outcome estimates are already signed to the hypothesis direction, so positive signed values mean the exposed group has a more negative CRISPR dependency score, i.e. stronger dependency. For outcome_014, a working 10%-scale benchmark is roughly 0.0093 because the absolute mean is about 0.093. H203/R170 is the broad envelope within feature_034=1: feature_042=1 versus feature_042=0 has signed estimate +0.058, interval +0.009 to +0.107. This is accepted but should not be read as a general feature_042 effect because the lower bound is at the benchmark and the pattern becomes much stronger in higher feature_024 strata. The clearest accepted contrast is H238/R205: within feature_034=1 and feature_024 at or above median, feature_042=1 versus feature_042=0 has signed estimate +0.104, interval +0.038 to +0.169. The lower bound far exceeds the outcome_014 benchmark, so this supports a clinically meaningful, stronger-dependency association in this dataset. H249/R216 refines the same feature_042 contrast to feature_034=1, feature_024 at or above median, and feature_045=0: +0.094, interval +0.019 to +0.169. H252/R219 gives the symmetric feature_034 contrast within feature_042=1 and feature_024 at or above median: +0.099, interval +0.016 to +0.183. H260/R232 narrows the feature_042 contrast to the upper feature_024 quartile within feature_034=1: +0.156, interval +0.062 to +0.249. These claims are not independent validations; they are nested and overlapping tests in the same 2000-observation dataset, but together they are consistent with a localized stronger-dependency pattern when feature_034 and feature_042 are both positive and feature_024 is high.

Negative or non-supported findings. The high feature_024 pattern is context-specific: H250/R217 tests feature_034=1 versus feature_034=0 within feature_042=0 and feature_024 at or above median and is near null: +0.002 interval -0.076 to +0.072. This supports specificity but is not proof of absence. H262/R234 tests the feature_042 contrast in the lower feature_024 quartile within feature_034=1: +0.008, interval -0.092 to +0.109, with no support for a clinically meaningful difference. H239/R206 in a lower feature_024 context is imprecise and unresolved, not evidence of absence. Several broader predictor claims were either null, underpowered, inconsistent, or failed independent validation. H1/R1 and validation R77 do not support a feature_002 outcome_001 association. H89 discovery suggested outcome_008 but validation R90 failed. H76/R151 suggested outcome_007 with feature_023, but validation R166 was null. H145 and validation R103 failed for outcome_006 feature_052. H146/R101 was rejected, and the reverse H148 plus validation R117 remains unresolved but not supported. H171 and especially H182/R143 versus validation R155 showed a promising feature_023 outcome_001 subgroup effect that did not replicate. H202/R169 discovery for outcome_001 feature_042 failed independent validation R179. These validation failures argue strongly against treating any broad or non-narrow predictor contrast as a reliable finding.

Unresolved uncertainty. The strongest unresolved signal is outcome_008. There are multiple interval-excluding-zero contrasts suggesting weaker dependency with feature_042=1 in feature_034 and high feature_024 contexts: H208/R174 +0.030 interval +0.005 to +0.054; H217/R188 +0.041 interval +0.008 to +0.075; H228/R199 +0.041 interval +0.002 to +0.079; H240/R207 +0.057 interval +0.007 to +0.108; H256/R228 +0.042 interval +0.006 to +0.078. However the working outcome_008 benchmark is about 0.0282, and these lower bounds are below it. Therefore the pattern is suggestive but not sufficient to claim a clinically meaningful association, especially after iterative subgroup selection. The direct upper-quartile specificity test for outcome_014, H261/R233, has a large point estimate but an interval lower bound near the benchmark and wide imprecision, so it remains unresolved. H253/R225, H254/R226, H255/R227, and other interaction leads do not robustly clear their benchmarks after multiplicity caution. H234/R220 is interval-supported for outcome_014 within feature_034=1 and feature_063=level_002, but I keep it unresolved because it is a post hoc feature_063 localization and no independent validation remains. Correlated outcome_006 extensions, including H265/R237, are too imprecise.

Next investigation. The most informative next analysis is not further mining of this dataset. If an external or pre-specified holdout cohort becomes available, test exactly the accepted outcome_014 contexts: feature_034=1 with feature_042=1 and feature_024 at or above median, the upper feature_024 quartile, and the feature_045=0 subset. Treat the finding as replicable only if the independent interval lower bound remains above the outcome_014 clinical benchmark of about 0.0093. Separately, outcome_008 should be reopened only if the exact feature_042 weaker-dependency contexts achieve an independent lower bound above about 0.0282. Any future supplied-dataset analysis should use pre-specified multiplicity control and, if possible, covariate adjustment; unadjusted Welch contrasts are adequate for descriptive associations here but not for causal inference.

results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.

Predictor names and text categorical values use opaque labels. Levels are nominal labels, not ordered numbers. Numeric values, outcome scales, and missingness are preserved.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

For outcome_014 proposals, raw exposed-minus-comparator differences are expected to be negative when the exposed condition has stronger dependency; registered direction -1 means returned signed estimates support stronger dependency when positive. evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
